what: Posts, rails, pickets and concrete for a wood fence
title: Fence Calculator: Posts, Rails, Pickets and Concrete | Calcupine
description: Free wood fence calculator. Enter the fence length and spacing to get posts, rails, pickets, screws and bags of concrete for setting posts.
lede: Enter the total fence length, post spacing and picket size. Get posts, rails, pickets, screws and the concrete to set the posts. The example is a 100 foot, 6 foot tall picket fence.

faq.q: How many fence posts do I need?
faq.a: Divide the fence length by the post spacing, round up, and add 1 for the end post. 100 feet with posts every 8 feet needs 14 posts. Add posts for gates and corners.

faq.q: How far apart should fence posts be?
faq.a: 6 to 8 feet is typical for wood fences; 8 feet matches standard rail length. Use closer spacing in windy areas or for heavy privacy fences.

faq.q: How deep should fence posts be?
faq.a: A common rule is about one third of the post's height above ground, and below your local frost line. Many 6 foot fences use holes 24 to 36 inches deep. Check local requirements.

faq.q: How many pickets do I need for 100 feet?
faq.a: With 5.5 inch pickets and a 1/2 inch gap, each picket covers 6 inches, so 100 feet (1,200 in) needs 200 pickets. A privacy fence with no gaps needs about 219.
